d2f5d19017d24057: SINGAPORE, Sept 16 — A 28-year-old woman has become the first person in Singapore to receive a custodial sentence for keeping animals in captivity for sale at unlicensed premises.
Such an act is an offence under Section 48(1) of the Animals and Birds Act, according to the National Parks Board (NParks) in a statement yesterday.

The case came to light after the woman, Ng Siew Teng, and her husband, Callurn Lim, 34, were arrested on December 27, 2023 for their involvement in a scheme to illegally import puppies from Malaysia for sale in Singapore.

The scheme was uncovered when Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA) officers found five smuggled puppies, including two in a pet carrier placed in a plastic storage container, during an inspection of a vehicle at Woodlands Checkpoint.
“Investigations found that the couple had kept illicitly imported puppies at their residence, and profited approximately S$21,000 (RM66,720) from selling 21 puppies through Instagram,” NParks said.

Ng and Lim pleaded guilty to five charges under the Animals and Birds Act and were each sentenced to 19 weeks and three days’ imprisonment and a fine of S$5,000 on August 5 and September 11, respectively.
This included a sentence of three days’ imprisonment and the maximum fine of S$5,000 for the Section 48(1) charge.
In a separate case, Sundra Pandian, 33, received the heaviest sentence to date for the same offence after 13 smuggled animals were found at his residence.
NParks said the animals were smuggled from Thailand through Malaysia by a transnational syndicate for sale in Singapore.
Pandian pleaded guilty to nine charges under the Animals and Birds Act and was sentenced to 24 weeks’ imprisonment on August 17.
The sentence included two weeks’ imprisonment for keeping animals in captivity for sale at unlicensed premises, the heaviest sentence meted out to date for the offence.
NParks said the case also involved Chow Chee Hoe, 25, who had facilitated the sale of the smuggled animals by collecting the animals from Pandian and selling them to prospective buyers in Singapore.
Chow pleaded guilty to one charge under the Animals and Birds (Licensing of Premises for Pet Shop and Other Purposes) Rules and was fined S$4,000 on September 1. — Bernama
e2b09ef3d0edd27b: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — The retail prices of RON97 petrol, unsubsidised RON95 petrol and unsubsidised diesel will each increase by 35 sen per litre for the Sept 17-23 period, the Ministry of Finance (MOF) said.

In a statement today, MOF said the retail price of RON97 would increase to RM4.85 per litre from RM4.50, while unsubsidised RON95 would rise to RM4.37 from RM4.02 and unsubsidised diesel to RM5.27 from RM4.92.
The ministry said the increase in global fuel prices was driven by heightened tensions in West Asia amid the conflict, which has entered its 200th day.

“Iran had attacked 10 vessels near the Strait of Hormuz in retaliation for US attacks on five Iranian tankers, while attacks also extended to Yemen and Saudi Arabia’s energy infrastructure. Vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz had fallen to single-digit levels following the surge in attacks.

“The situation worsened after drone attacks forced the temporary suspension of operations along Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline, which is among the key routes bypassing the Strait of Hormuz,” the statement said.
MOF said these developments drove Brent crude oil prices back above US$100 per barrel, reaching nearly US$110 per barrel during the Automatic Pricing Mechanism (APM) calculation period.

At the same time, the ministry said disruptions to refining capacity in Russia and constraints on crude oil supplies continued to limit the production of refined petroleum products, keeping refining margins high and putting upward pressure on global petroleum prices.
According to MOF, escalating tensions in West Asia and the Russia-Ukraine conflict could result in prolonged volatility in global petroleum prices.

Meanwhile, MOF said the Madani Government would continue to protect the people and businesses from the impact of global uncertainties, including by maintaining targeted BUDI Madani subsidies for eligible consumers.
Under BUDI95, eligible recipients will continue to pay RM1.99 per litre for RON95, with the government bearing a subsidy of RM2.38 per litre, or 54 per cent of the unsubsidised price of RM4.37.
For BUDI Diesel, recipients will pay RM2.10 per litre, with the government providing a subsidy of RM3.17 per litre, or 60 per cent of the unsubsidised price of RM5.27.

The basic monthly eligibility limit for BUDI95 and BUDI Diesel was raised again to 300 litres effective Sept 1, while eligible owners of diesel-powered pickup trucks and jeeps would receive an additional 100 litres, bringing their total monthly eligibility to 400 litres, the ministry said.

“The Madani Government will continue to take a prudent approach to protect the people from price fluctuations while ensuring the nation’s fuel supply remains sufficient and secure,” the statement read. — Bernama
6a2846e710a205bc: STRASBOURG, Sept 16 — EU chief Ursula von der Leyen raised the prospect today of Canada becoming the 27-nation bloc’s first “associate member’, as she pitched closer cooperation on tech, defence and energy to Canadian leader Mark Carney.
Von der Leyen told the European Parliament in Strasbourg that, as democracies face a “fracture in the international rules-based system”, Brussels and Ottawa needed to pull closer together.

“I would like to work with you on opening the door for Canada to be the first associate member of the EU,” von der Leyen told the Canadian prime minister, who was attending her annual keynote speech — drawing a standing ovation in the chamber.
Carney has been pursuing closer ties with the European Union, as both seek to pivot away from a hostile United States under President Donald Trump.

The first foreign head of government to attend the annual “State of the European Union” speech — before addressing the parliament himself the next day — his visit is meant to act as a catalyst ahead of an EU-Canada summit in Montreal next month.
Von der Leyen said it was time to move from cooperation based on trade to a broader “alliance for the future” and “bring the relationship with Canada to the highest level possible”.
“We will work on intelligent manufacturing. We will create a tech alliance. We will integrate defence industrial bases. We will make the Arctic a flagship joint project,” she said.
She listed energy, critical minerals, batteries, AI, cyber and economic security, as other fields of cooperation.
“This is a partnership not against anyone else, but for our common strength,” she added.
What’s in a name
EU treaties do not envision the possibility of becoming an “associate member”. But the idea was first floated by German Chancellor Friedrich Merz this year vis-a-vis Ukraine.

Under that plan, which met a cold reception in Kyiv as it pushes for full membership, Ukraine would have been allowed to attend the bloc’s summits and have a representative in the European Commission.
It would have also benefited from parts of the EU budget, but without full voting rights.

“We don’t really know yet what it means,” said Tobias Cremer, a centre-left European lawmaker from Germany and the main sponsor of a March resolution urging stronger EU-Canada cooperation, after von der Leyen’s “associate membership” pitch.
But a closer alliance “inherently” made sense, he added. “Not just because we share values and history but because we share common interests, we share a strategic vision,” he told AFP.

Valerie Hayer, the head of the centrist Renew group, envisaged an even broader partnership as she took the floor after von der Leyen, telling lawmakers Ottawa and Brussels must respond together to tariffs and “trade coercion”, and foster university exchanges among other things.
Others were less enthusiastic.
“Who has given you a democratic and popular mandate to do that?” Manon Aubry, a French lawmaker from the Left group asked von der Leyen.
Under EU rules, member states have to approve any form of partnership with a third country and it was unclear how much support von der Leyen’s proposal would receive from capitals.
‘Shared future’
Buffeted by US tariffs and competition from China, Brussels and Ottawa already enjoy a considerable level of cooperation.
A free-trade agreement (CETA) that abolished almost all tariffs has been credited with boosting trade in goods and services by more than 80 per cent since 2016.
And this year Canada became the first non-EU country to join a flagship defence loan programme.

On Tuesday, Canada’s ambassador to the EU Jonathan Wilkinson cited a deal to ship Canadian liquefied natural gas (LNG) to Germany, and Canadian AI firm Cohere’s investments in the same European country, as examples that could inspire broader collaboration.
Ottawa was also hoping to get over the line a deal allowing the European Investment Bank (EIB) to put money behind Canadian critical minerals projects, he told AFP.
Carney was to hold talks with von der Leyen today before flying to Britain for his first meeting with Britain’s new prime minister, Andy Burnham.
He will also attend a Premier League football match between Everton and Wolverhampton before returning to Strasbourg ahead of his Thursday speech.
“We believe that power does not belong to the strongest, the richest or the loudest — but to all of us. That democracies have the freedom to choose with whom to work,” von der Leyen said.
“We share one ocean, one set of values, one way of seeing the world. And we will now build our shared future as well,” she concluded. — AFP

6cc453e45e585739: KUALA LUMPUR: Selangor MCA has called on the government to fully recognise the Unified Examination Certificate (UEC) for admission to public universities and employment in the civil service.

In a resolution adopted at its 2026 state convention, the party urged Putrajaya to “fulfil its election promises as soon as possible” by granting full recognition to the UEC through a “fair, transparent and standardised” mechanism.
In May, the government decided that UEC graduates could pursue their studies at public higher learning institutions.

However, the programmes available to them are limited to the following: bachelor of arts in Chinese language studies with honours; bachelor’s degree in Chinese language and linguistics; bachelor of arts in Chinese studies; and bachelor’s degree in Chinese language with education.
Selangor MCA also called for a review of admission mechanisms for STPM, matriculation and foundation programmes, as well as the public university admission system (UPU).
The party said admissions should be based on academic performance and merit, with qualified students given equal opportunities.

“The government must ensure that all qualified students are given equal opportunities and publicly disclose admission data, quota allocations and selection criteria for all higher education pathways,” the resolution said.
After the convention, Selangor MCA chief Lawrence Low told reporters that about 630 members turned up for the event, which discussed politics, party affairs, education, culture and the economy.

During the convention, he said there were also calls to review Selangor's guidelines on non-Muslim houses of worship following public complaints about the demolition of places of worship and parking issues.
He said a special committee headed by Petaling Jaya MCA youth chief Andy Teoh would look into the legal aspects of the guidelines and the complaints.
Selangor MCA also urged the state government to consult pig farmers and industry operators over existing livestock farming policies and provide compensation and assistance to those affected.
“The government should assist industry operators in making an orderly transition to other suitable livestock sectors,” it said.
The call comes after the Selangor government imposed a statewide ban on pig farming earlier this year, with existing farms ordered to cease operations in stages.

On the economy, Selangor MCA called for the goods and services tax to replace the sales and service tax and e-invoice system, and proposed a cross-sector special economic committee to coordinate the government’s response to global economic risks and external shocks.
It also called for tighter verification and monitoring of foreign nationals and refugees, particularly the Rohingya, as well as a review of the migrant worker recruitment system.
251038ac49165d12: QINZHOU: The Pinglu Canal, a key project of the New International Land-Sea Trade Corridor, officially opened to shipping today, creating a new water transport corridor linking southwestern China with Asean and international markets.
The canal is also a landmark project in China’s efforts to build a transportation powerhouse.

Spanning 134.2km, the canal starts from the Pingtang Estuary in the Xijin Reservoir area of Hengzhou, Nanning, and enters the Beibu Gulf along the Qinjiang River through Luwu Town in Lingshan County, Qinzhou.

Wei Minxin, the engineer of the Pinglu Canal project, said the opening of the canal not only strengthens transport connectivity but also contributes to closer ties between China and Asean countries. The canal connects with the railway network in southwestern China and the Beibu Gulf port network, forming an integrated transport system involving waterways, railways and maritime routes, he added.
“Pinglu Canal serves as a major project and key hub of the New Western Land-Sea Trade Corridor,” he told reporters at the site here today.

Built to Class I inland waterway standards, the canal can accommodate vessels of up to 5,000 tonnes and, with shipping as its primary function, the project also integrates water supply, irrigation, flood prevention and aquatic environmental improvement. The project, which began construction in August 2022, has an estimated budget of about 72.7 billion yuan.

The Pinglu Canal provides a shorter, more economical and convenient water transport corridor from Guangxi and southwestern China to the Asean region. The new route is expected to reduce the inland river transport distance for goods by more than 560km compared with traditional routes.

The project is expected to accelerate the transformation of regional resources into economic strengths and promote the development of cross-border and trans-regional industrial and supply chains linking the Asean region, Beibu Gulf Economic Zone, Chengdu-Chongqing Economic Zone and Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area.

The canal is expected to serve as a strategic hub for China’s domestic and international dual-circulation development strategy, while contributing to the development of Guangxi and the broader western region.

The opening of the canal will also enable the Beibu Gulf Port to further develop from a seaport into a multimodal transport hub connecting southwestern China with domestic and international markets. The project incorporates a three-tier water-saving basin system, which can reduce water consumption by more than 60%.

The Pinglu Canal also connects the new trade route with the China-Europe Railway Express network and cross-border shipping routes, further expanding China’s logistics connectivity with Asean countries.

ee52adc0ac762772: KUALA LUMPUR: Angkatan Tentera Malaysia (ATM) bakal melakar sejarah dengan menubuhkan Angkatan Siber sebagai ketumbukan keempatnya menjelang 2030 bagi mendepani ancaman landskap keselamatan moden.

Panglima ATM Malek Razak Sulaiman berkata, langkah strategik itu diambil memandangkan ruang siber dan elektromagnetik kini menjadi medan persaingan serta pertempuran yang semakin mendominasi pada peringkat global.

Beliau berkata, satu pasukan khusus dikenali sebagai Tim Nukleus Angkatan Siber telah diwujudkan untuk menerajui aspek perancangan, penyelarasan, persediaan transformasi organisasi dan pembangunan keupayaan ke arah penubuhan rasmi angkatan tersebut.

Katanya, pelancaran tim nukleus itu dijadual disempurnakan oleh Menteri Pertahanan Khaled Nordin bersempena dengan sambutan Karnival Hari ATM 2026 di Pangkalan Tentera Laut Diraja Malaysia (TLDM) Lumut, Perak pada 19 Sept ini.

"Kita melihat model daripada negara jiran dan asing yang telah pun menerapkan domain ini dalam ketumbukan mereka, jadi keperluan ini amat mendesak dan kita tidak boleh tertinggal," katanya dalam temu bual khas bersempena dengan sambutan Hari ATM ke-93.

"Pasukan nukleus ini akan merancang serta melihat bagaimana untuk merealisasikan Angkatan Siber ini menjadi kenyataan dan beroperasi sepenuhnya selari dengan garis panduan kementerian untuk direalisasikan menjelang 2030."
Mengulas lanjut, Malek Razak berkata, selari dengan hasrat tersebut, ATM juga melaksanakan pembangunan kepakaran dalam bidang Aktiviti Siber dan Elektromagnetik (Cema) secara berterusan.

Katanya, keupayaan siber, peperangan elektronik dan operasi pengurusan spektrum itu telah pun diaplikasikan secara praktikal bagi menghasilkan kesan operasi yang nyata menerusi Eksesais Camar Kilat Siri 2/26.
"Komitmen ini turut diperkukuh menerusi aspek modal insan, dengan sebanyak 60 pegawai dan 17 anggota lain-lain pangkat TUDM telah mengikuti kursus berkaitan Cema hingga Julai lepas," katanya.

Sebelum ini, Khaled dilaporkan berkata, Kementerian Pertahanan kini dalam peringkat merangka usaha membangunkan Pasukan Siber sebagai perkhidmatan atau pasukan keempat bagi menangani ancaman peperangan moden dan kognitif.

Beliau berkata, langkah itu diambil memandangkan ancaman pada masa kini tidak lagi terhad kepada pertempuran fizikal secara tradisional semata-mata, sebaliknya mula beralih kepada penguasaan ruang siber dan persepsi masyarakat.
a4af1681697ea433: Logitech has released the MX Keypad, a developer-focused keypad derived from its MX Creative Console, and something that triggers a distinct sense of déjà vu. Do you remember Stack Overflow's "The Key" Joke? Three keys to copy and paste code from the developer's former best friend (until AI tools began to eat its lunch). Logitech took the keypad from its MX Creative Console product and made something similar to Stack Overflow's joke-that-became-a-thing, though considerably more extensible. The company sent us one to look at, and it's an interesting, if perhaps slightly expensive, bit of kit. At its heart, the MX Keypad is a set of nine keys that can trigger commands. Out of the box, it all looks a bit bland – there are monochrome images on the keys for playback, volume, screenshot taking, and even something to bring up an emoji panel when attached to a Windows device. However, things get a good deal more colorful and interesting when the device is connected to the Logi Options+ application. Then the device moves from being a curiosity to something that threatens to be indispensable, depending on your workflow. Using Word to knock out some writing? The MX Keypad will show a bunch of commonly used commands, or you can customize it to suit your workflow. How about Visual Studio Code? It's the same again – the keys light up with some default commands that you can easily make your own. According to Logitech, the device is a "Multi-App AI Control Center for Developers" and was developed in conjunction with keyboard jockeys. We'd call it a surprisingly useful bit of kit which has rapidly become part of our workflow, both for productivity and when diving into VS Code for some source wrangling. There are, of course, downsides. Although the price is relatively competitive, it is a little on the high side for what is ultimately a smart macro keypad. It also requires a USB-C connection, which we can understand given the power needs of those bright, backlit, color LCDs, but it would have been nice if Logitech could have come up with something that didn't need a cable. And, of course, you need Logitech's software to get the best out of it. In the box is the keypad itself, a USB-C cable, and a stand. We preferred to position it on the desk next to the keyboard for ease of access – the device has a slightly angled base, so it works well in that placement, but the inclusion of a stand is a nice touch. There's also an SDK if engineers (or their agents) wish to get their hands dirty, and a marketplace where plugins for the likes of Claude Code and OpenAI Codex can be found. According to Logitech, these give developers "real-time agent status tracking and CLI control right on the physical keys." Assuming you can make it work. We found the Logi Options+ software a little unintuitive and recommend some perseverance to get the best out of it, along with a little caution, since the built-in designer can create some deeply wince-inducing key designs. Ultimately, the MX Keypad represents some excellent repurposing by Logitech. The original MX Creative Console was useful for creative types, but its jog wheel was arguably of little use to developers. The touch panel, with its customizable keys, is a much more practical proposition; by selling it on its own, Logitech has cut the price to £89.99 ($99.99). It comes in light or dark gray and has a pleasingly quality feel. Having to plug it in is annoying, given the wireless nature of many other peripherals, and you do need to get to grips with the Logitech Options+ application to get the best out of it, but once it forms part of your workflow, it becomes a hard habit to break. ®
8be311a9b438a797: KUALA LUMPUR: The professionalism and capabilities of the armed forces came to the fore on the world stage when it made history as the first military force from Asia to participate in a North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) mission through the Implementation Force (IFOR), a peace enforcement force, in Bosnia in 1995.

Armed forces veteran Major General (Rtd) Datuk Mohamad Raih Ismail said that before being accepted to participate in the more challenging IFOR mission, the Malaysian contingent first underwent rigorous tests by NATO.

He said that during the transition from the peacekeeping force to IFOR, the MAF successfully relocated 1,533 personnel, along with hundreds of vehicles, including Condor armoured vehicles, in heavy snowfall and sub-zero temperatures.

"The movement, which took a month, was completed without a single accident," he said this while sharing his experience under the topic 'Veteran ATM: Mewarisi Kehebatan, Memperkasa Masa Hadapan' during the Apa Khabar Malaysia programme produced by Bernama TV today.
He said the achievement also attracted the attention of the British military, which was impressed as its own forces had recorded accidents and fatalities while facing extreme weather conditions.

Raih also shared his experience of the country contingent's participation in Operation United Shield in Somalia in 1995, which saw Task Force Malaysia deployed with two ships, KD Mahawangsa and KD Inderasakti, to protect the withdrawal mission of United Nations (UN) peacekeepers under UNOSOM II.

He said the operation was carried out alongside military forces from seven countries, including the United States, Italy and France, and was successfully completed on March 2, 1995, without any problems.
"The best experience we gained was proving that our forces could work with other foreign military forces at a very professional level," he said.
Raih joined the armed forces in 1970 after being commissioned into the Royal Malay Regiment, and served in various roles as staff and commander at company, battalion, brigade and division levels.
He also served as assistant defence attaché in the Philippines during the People Power Revolution.

20ed7866eb1370ab: KUCHING: Malaysia and Indonesia have agreed to cooperate in tackling transboundary haze, which has affected air quality in several countries in the region.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he discussed the issue with Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto while in New Delhi, India, recently.

"Yes, it was raised. We will cooperate to reduce the impact of transboundary haze," he told reporters after the official handover of Bintulu Port from the Federal Government to the Sarawak Government at Kuching International Airport here today.
Anwar was responding to questions about his meeting with Prabowo on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit in New Delhi.
He declined to elaborate, saying he was rushing to the Borneo Kuching Convention Centre (BCCK) to attend Malaysia Day celebrations.
Meanwhile, the takeover of Bintulu Port by the Sarawak Government followed negotiations between the two governments before the deal was finalised in June.
On June 21, Sarawak completed a RM1.8 billion payment to the Federal Government for the transfer of ownership, assets and responsibilities related to the port.
The Sarawak Government officially took over the management and administration of Bintulu Port on Sept 1, following the repeal of the Bintulu Port Authority Act, which came into effect on Aug 31.

The official handover today was carried out by Transport Minister Anthony Loke to Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas, witnessed by Anwar and Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Abang Openg.

The transfer of Bintulu Port from a federal to a state port is seen as a significant development in the implementation of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63), as well as reflecting cooperation and understanding between the Federal Government and Sarawak.
6ae4aa73526174fc: THE HAGUE, Sept 16 — Former Philippines president Rodrigo Duterte appeared in person at the International Criminal Court for the first time today, as he faces charges over his “war on drugs” that killed thousands.
The 81-year-old had appeared by video link when he was first brought to the court in The Hague, but had since skipped hearings, with his defence team saying he was too ill.
Dressed in a dark suit and white shirt with no tie, the former president sat with his chin resting on his hands as proceedings opened.
Judge Joanna Korner noted his appearance in court for the first time, and said he could leave the court at any time without seeking permission from the bench.
But he stayed throughout the hearing, which lasted one hour and 15 minutes, showing no emotion and seeming to follow proceedings through headphones.
Duterte did not speak during the hearing but waved at the public gallery when the judge had left the courtroom at the end.
He is the first Asian former head of state to face trial at the ICC, which prosecutes individuals for the world’s worst crimes such as war crimes and crimes against humanity.
Duterte faces three counts of crimes against humanity, with prosecutors alleging his involvement in at least 76 murders between 2013 and 2018 during his offensive against drug users and sellers.
Korner has set November 30 as the start date of the trial, which could take months or even years.
The only time Duterte had been seen since his arrest in March 2025 was an initial appearance via video, where he seemed confused and tired, his speech barely audible.
‘It’s impossible’
Today’s hearing was a “status hearing” for the parties and the judge to fix logistical details.
Lawyers clashed over evidence filed by the prosecution, which they said was around 15,000 pieces but the defence put at more than 62,000 documents.
“It’s quite enormous. It’s impossible,” said defence lawyer Peter Haynes. “We haven’t got a prayer of reading” such a mountain of documents before the trial starts, said Haynes.
“The current state of the case is a mess. If I had a younger, healthier client, I would invite you to put back the trial by six months... but I don’t,” said Duterte’s lawyer.
Korner chided the prosecution for “wholesale dumping” of documents and urged the parties to work together to reduce the size of the case file.
Relatives of some of those killed in the anti-drugs campaign welcomed Duterte’s appearance in court.

Randy Delos Santos, 48, an uncle of Kian Delos Santos, a teenager killed by police in August 2017, when Duterte was president, told AFP: “Of course, we are very happy that he is now able to attend in person.
“We hope that his being physically fit will help speed up the hearings,” Santos told AFP in Manila.
In a submission published yesterday, Duterte’s lawyers said he suffered from “significant memory impairment that prevents him from retaining recent information and reliably accessing memories”.
Judges are weighing whether he is mentally fit to be tried and have ordered a medical assessment by three experts.
That assessment has not been made public but Duterte’s defence cited the results of examinations contained in the report.
According to the defence, these examination showed Duterte thinks he is living in 2007 or 2008, that he is 84 or 85 years old, and could not recall the name of the current US president.
‘Bluster and hyperbole’
During hearings in February, the prosecution alleged Duterte killed thousands of suspected drug dealers and users, first as mayor of Davao City, then as president.

The true number of killings during his campaign in the Philippines is thought to be in the thousands, and lawyers for the victims have argued that a full trial could encourage more families to come forward.
His then defence lawyer Nicolas Kaufman told the court in February his client “absolutely” maintained his innocence.
Kaufman told ICC judges the evidence against Duterte was “wholly insufficient” and the charges “grievously misplaced and politically motivated”.
He argued that while Duterte used “bluster and hyperbole” in his speeches, he also frequently ordered authorities only to shoot in self-defence.
Duterte remains popular in the Philippines, where many favoured his tough approach to crime. — AFP

a6f49c53d44395e1: BEIRUT: Lebanese president Joseph Aoun told AFP in an exclusive interview he wants a security agreement with Israel once it withdraws its troops as a possible prelude to peace, and is determined to disarm Hezbollah without a confrontation.

Speaking ahead of his departure to France on Wednesday, president Joseph Aoun said Lebanon wanted a new force, European or otherwise, to prevent a security vacuum after UN peacekeepers leave south Lebanon when their mandate expires at the end of the year.
He called on the US, EU and Arab countries to support Lebanon's military as it deploys across the country.
Lebanon under Aoun has committed to disarming Iran-backed Hezbollah, which dragged the country into the wider Middle East war by attacking Israel earlier this year.

Aoun said he wants a security agreement with Israel "primarily to end the state of hostility and the deployment of the army on the border. This could be a prelude to a later peace agreement, but we cannot jump directly to a peace agreement".
"We have no choice but negotiations, because the alternative is war, which would be very costly for us," he added.

In Paris, Aoun will attend a meeting hosted by President Emmanuel Macron and attended by King Abdullah II of Jordan to build international support for Lebanese troops as they deploy across the country.
"Our Arab and European partners, as well as the United States and our friends, must share with us the responsibility of supporting the army and strengthening the Lebanese state," he said.
Aoun reiterated Lebanon was determined to disarm Hezbollah, saying the decision was "neither negotiable nor open to discussion".
Hezbollah has long maintained a massive arsenal that it has used to fight repeated wars with Israel, while exerting an outsized role in Lebanese politics.
Critics have accused the Iran-backed militants of keeping Lebanon locked in a cycle of violence, while preventing the state from functioning fully across the country.
Speaking to AFP, Aoun struck a conciliatory tone in his remarks on Hezbollah and the push to disarm it.
"The objective is not a confrontation," he said. "We are determined to resolve this issue peacefully.
"This is not about building a state at the cost of a bloody conflict... or a new civil war."
Decades on from the end of a civil war that killed 150,000 people, Lebanon remains deeply divided and still lives under the spectre of internal conflict.
'No vacuum'
Aoun said he had told Iran that relations "must be based on mutual respect and non-interference in the internal affairs of the Lebanese people.
"We have no problem with having a relationship with Iran, but we do have a problem with interference in our internal affairs."
Under US pressure, the UN Security Council voted last year to end the mandate of the UN peacekeeping force in south Lebanon on December 31, 2026.
Unifil, currently involving around 7,500 peacekeepers from nearly 50 countries, has been deployed since 1978.

"What matters is that there is no vacuum," Aoun told AFP on Tuesday. He added that any new force for Lebanon's south, part of which is occupied by Israel, would be "temporary until the (Lebanese) army can deploy".
"Whatever the nature of this force, that poses no problem for me: European, non-European, American, another United Nations force, Asian, or even a mix of European, Arab and Asian forces," Aoun said.
He has repeatedly urged the international community to extend the mandate of the peacekeepers, who have witnessed war after war in south Lebanon since the mission was first deployed.
"The best and most optimal option remains extending Unifil's mandate," he added.
Asked about Israel's upcoming election, Aoun said it was an internal matter.
"But the question we want to ask the Israeli people, the State of Israel and all future governments is the following: do they want stability, security and no wars on their border, or not?" he said.

ef0f09132d707ac6: BERA: Orang Asli villagers living near Tasek Bera are seeking negotiations with the authorities after receiving notices in June ordering them to vacate parts of the forest reserve, saying the land has been their source of livelihood for generations.

Now facing eviction, they want a dialogue with the authorities, hoping their long-standing ties to the customary land (tanah adat) will be taken into consideration.
Enforcement team members attempted to enter several villages and smallholdings, including Kampung Pathir, on Sept 14 but were stopped by villagers who had erected barriers.
The tense situation at Kampung Pathir, about 10am, led to the arrest of five people, including four women.

Kampung Pathir Tok Batin Amir Noor Tan, 49, said several Orang Asli villages around Tasek Bera received pink warning notices from the Forestry Department in June for allegedly encroaching into the permanent forest reserve.
"We lodged a police report before setting up guard posts at all the village entrances and smallholdings around Tasek Bera... we have people stationed at the posts around the clock.

"We met Pahang Orang Asli Affairs Committee chairman Datuk Seri Syed Ibrahim Syed Ahmad in Temerloh to seek the withdrawal of the notices, while all the village headmen jointly sent a letter to the Menteri Besar's office asking it to look into the matter, but no action was taken," he said when met at the settlement today.
Amir Noor said several enforcement agencies led by the Pahang State Enforcement Unit arrived on Sept 14 and conducted drone surveillance of the area.
"They did not seek our permission or mention that they would be measuring our land.
"The situation became tense when the enforcement team tried to enter the village. Some refused to give in, which led to the arrest of five villagers here," he said.
Amir Noor said the enforcement team had yet to return to Kampung Pathir, adding that he was informed they had gone to other settlements near the lake today.
He said more than 7,000 Orang Asli lived in 11 settlements surrounding the lake, which he described as the main settlement area for the Semelai tribe in Pahang.
"All the villagers are connected to Tasik Bera, Sungai Bera and Sungai Serting. What are we going to do if our smallholdings within the forest reserve are taken away?" he said.
He added that Kampung Pathir had not received the notice, although enforcement team members had already entered the settlement.
Amir Noor expressed frustration over the incident, saying the Tok Batin used to be the first person consulted before authorities entered a village.
"These days, it is as though we (Tok Batin) no longer exist and our roles are being sidelined," he said, claiming none of the villages near the lake had been gazetted as Orang Asli villages.
He also dismissed claims on social media that the Orang Asli community in Tasek Bera had been instigated by outsiders to rebel against the authorities.

"We do not need third parties to advise us on the matter, as our families have lived here for a long time, even before Tasek Bera was gazetted as a Ramsar site," he said, adding that they previously planted padi near the lake.
The New Straits Times visited several settlements near Tasek Bera today. Most had guard posts, although many villagers appeared reluctant to speak.
Meanwhile, mother-of-three Zaitun Gosi, 60, said the villagers would have no land to work on if the forest reserve land was taken over by the state authorities.
"Please have some mercy on us. We have been staying here for a long time. Why are we only now being told to vacate our land in the forest reserve?" she said.
Villager Lama Kaya, 60, said the development was disturbing for the Orang Asli community living by the lake, as their future was now uncertain.
"The authorities should speak to us and explain what they are planning to do with our land," he said.

A copy of the Forestry Department notice dated June 25, 2026, sighted by the NST stated that the offence was committed under Section 81(g) of the National Forestry Act 1985 for allegedly trespassing into a permanent forest reserve without authorisation.
The notice ordered the occupants to vacate the area within 14 days.

NST has reached out to Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail's office, Syed Ibrahim and Pahang Orang Asli Development Department (Jakoa) director Adam Zaidi Mahidin for their responses to the enforcement operation.

Meanwhile, Kemayan assemblyman Khaizulnizam Mohd Zuldin told the New Straits Times that Pahang Orang Asli Affairs Committee chairman Datuk Seri Syed Ibrahim Syed Ahmad had recently visited villages around Tasek Bera.
"As far as I am concerned, the Orang Asli community near Tasek Bera can continue to occupy their homes. The Pahang government is prepared to listen to and study their needs.

"I believe there is still room for discussions on the matter, as we do not want the issue to be politicised. We must be careful when dealing with land matters as they are sensitive," he said when contacted.

Khaizulnizam said the Pahang government would uphold the decree of the Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah, that the Orang Asli community must not be misled into believing that every area they claim as "customary land" (tanah adat) automatically belongs to them.

a21a585632974521: PARIS, Sept 16 — The mayor of Paris today expressed his “deepest regrets” over multiple cases of physical and sexual assault on children by school staff, admitting there had been a lack of transparency in handling the crisis.

Parents in the French capital have been deeply unsettled by the scandal which saw multiple allegations of sexual or physical violence emerge in recent months against monitors the city employs to look after children outside the classroom, such as during lunchtime, after lessons or in holiday camps.

“I wish to express my deepest regrets. Personal regrets first, but also those of the city of Paris, which I represent in an official capacity,” Emmanuel Gregoire told a fact-finding inquiry of the upper house Senate.

Gregoire, elected mayor earlier this year to succeed his fellow Socialist Anne Hidalgo who held the post for 12 years, acknowledged that the city of Paris may have “lacked transparency,” particularly because “public meetings with parents and advocacy groups were not held systematically”.

Like Hidalgo, who appeared before the inquiry yesterday, he appeared to stop short of issuing a personal apology, saying that the city of Paris “never failed to meet the legal recruitment obligations”.
The comments by Gregoire, who had previously served as Hidalgo’s first deputy mayor, came a day after a Paris court imposed the heaviest sentence since the allegations emerged.

Michael M., 38, admitted during his trial to having sexually assaulted nine children aged five to 10 between September 2022 and January 2024. The court handed him a five-year term, four of which were suspended, and ordered him to serve the one-year term under house arrest with an ankle tag.

Prosecutors are investigating whether Gregoire and Hidalgo should be held responsible after parents filed several complaints alleging mismanagement. Since the start of the year, Paris has suspended 132 aides, including 52 suspected of sexual abuse. — AFP

3deaf2be0e1dcccb: TypeSafe, founded by a ChatGPT co-inventor, has left stealth and is launching its Jev model to automate programmatic decisions with parallel sampling architecture.

Software systems requiring automated deterministic logic can now bypass conversational language models following TypeSafe AI’s release of Jev, a specialised System One Model designed to execute structured probabilistic decisions directly inside production codebases.
Developed during two years in stealth by OpenAI veteran and ChatGPT co-inventor Diogo Almeida, the model abandons text and string generation entirely.

Instead of autoregressively generating sequential text tokens, the system takes an unstructured state as an input and outputs type-safe structured values in a single parallel query. The architecture targets deterministic code integration, preventing syntactic type failures and output hallucinations by design.
Diogo Almeida, Founder at TypeSafe, said: “Think of Jev as a frontier-intelligence function call: unstructured state in, typed probabilistic decisions out.”
Jev model architecture: How hardware-aware parallel sampling works
Engineers built the platform around an alternative training methodology termed Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions (RLCD).

Conventional frontier models train via Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF) or Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) to satisfy human conversational preferences or isolated programmatic checks. TypeSafe trains Jev to produce calibrated probabilities on execution logic, ensuring returned confidence scores correlate directly with output accuracy.
Departing from autoregressive token generation, Jev relies on a hardware-aware parallel sampler that evaluates and delivers all structured values simultaneously.

The structural constraint restricts outputs to predefined schemas, eliminating the parsing pipelines and guardrail wrappers required when deploying traditional large language models across business automation flows. The internal sampler handles high-cardinality selections up to 255 discrete options, using a two-stage process that scores options independently prior to selection.

Internal evaluations conducted from the team’s West Coast servers record end-to-end response latencies between 70–500 milliseconds, contrasted against the 3–329 seconds observed across conversational frontier deployments.

Published workflow evaluations run across fixed compute graphs (measuring multi-step decision branching against consensus baselines from GPT-6 Astra and Fable 5.1) recorded execution speeds up to 193.6 times faster.

Input processing costs are priced at $0.042 per million tokens, down from standard conversational rates spanning $0.20 to $10 per million tokens. Because parallel sampling generates structured states without autoregressive token generation passes, TypeSafe provides output tokens without metering charges.
From Doom bots to petabyte data: Real-world Jev deployment testing

Production demonstrations show Jev resolving branching rules across high-speed game states and web traversal trees. In dynamic stress testing, engineers operated a real-time reactive bot across Doom game state structures at 10 queries per second, generating operating costs of approximately $7 per hour.

A secondary Wikiracing test evaluated link selection across dense encyclopaedia directories, finishing traversals in fewer steps than external non-reasoning models by evaluating options without generating hallucinated dead ends.

Field testing confirms primary target applications across real-time feature extraction, petabyte-scale data workflows, output verification layers, and automated branching logic where hand-written rules prove brittle.
TypeSafe opened early developer access today and started onboarding engineering teams from its deployment waitlist.

25306525b70b7b11: STRASBOURG: The European Union will ban social media for children under 13 and allow only limited, supervised access until the age of 15 under plans unveiled Wednesday by EU chief Ursula von der Leyen.
A global backlash against social media has piled pressure on policymakers, with a rising body of evidence showing negative impacts on children's physical and mental health.
Australia last year became the first country to ban social media for under-16s, triggering a wave of similar moves elsewhere.
The 27-country bloc would take a "gradual" approach, von der Leyen confirmed during her annual keynote address to the European Parliament in Strasbourg, France.
"Each age has its own sensitivities. And therefore, each will have its own tailored protection level," she said.

"No social media under the age of 13. No personal account under the age of 15," she said. "That means from 13 to under 15, only mini accounts, set up and supervised by parents or guardians, with limited features and time restriction to one hour a day."
"And between 15 and 18, safe design will be an obligation for the platforms."

Before she outlined the EU's approach, von der Leyen paid tribute to a 14-year-old girl in Belgium, named Olea, who killed herself one month ago after being bullied, and whose mother she quoted as saying: "I am convinced that without these omnipresent networks, my daughter would still be here."
Von der Leyen made no reference to online games or AI chatbots, which according to draft legislation seen by AFP would also be hit by the restrictions.
The European Commission president and tech chief Henna Virkkunen will formally present the proposed "KIDS Act", including the tiered age limits in Strasbourg, France on Thursday.
The EU will also ban addictive design features such as so-called infinite scrolling where children are concerned, according to a draft document.
If platforms break the rules, they face fines of up to 6% of annual turnover, draft details show.
"Europe has the power to act. It is we who decide our rules, not big tech," von der Leyen said.
"We do not have to accept addictive features," she warned, saying "platforms will have to prove that they are safe".
"It is not about our minors accessing social media. It is about when and how do we allow social media to access minors," von der Leyen added.

The "risk" is not limited to children, she noted. "Addictive design, for example, is harming everyone," she said, telling EU lawmakers that Europe needed more rules that will be proposed in the autumn.
Pressure from EU states
Among those listening in the grand chamber was Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney whose country has also moved to curb social media for under-16s.
Von der Leyen had faced pressure from member states including France, Denmark and Greece for action across the 27-nation bloc to limit online harms for children.
The EU has sought for years to rein in Big Tech, empowering itself with a strengthened legal armoury that it now believes is not sufficient.

The bloc has already told Meta platforms Facebook and Instagram as well as TikTok to change their "addictive" design through its content law known as the Digital Services Act, but changes have taken longer than Brussels wants.
Digital and children's rights groups have raised concerns over how the new social media curbs will work in practice, as well as over a related age-check app the EU is preparing to roll out.
"Age verification is not a silver bullet and would raise serious privacy and data protection concerns," said European consumer organisation BEUC's Agustin Reyna.
Thursday's proposal will only become law after negotiations on a final text between EU capitals and the European Parliament, which could take months.

6b9b3fc2a3ac6f93: BATU PAHAT: MCA is ready to face the 16th General Election (GE16) earlier than scheduled, party president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong said.
Wee said there was no guarantee the government would wait until the full five-year term was up before calling the election, based on the track record of previous general elections.

"I have already said in my speech that we actually need to shift into fifth gear now. We must always be prepared — not the kind of preparation where we only get ready today because we are going to contest tomorrow.
"MCA must ensure that election machinery and strategies are put in place early, including taking into account the different political conditions in each state," he said.
He said MCA's approach could not be standardised across all states, as Johor, Negri Sembilan and Melaka each had different political characteristics and varying levels of party strength.
"Each state has its own strategy. Johor is different from Negeri Sembilan, so we have to work harder in each state according to its own mould.
"We need to identify where our strengths lie, which areas we can win, and we must conduct a precise analysis," he said.
He was speaking after officiating the MCA Johor Annual Convention in Yong Peng here.
Wee, who is also the Ayer Hitam member of Parliament, said MCA had shown improvement following its performance in the recent Johor and Negeri Sembilan state elections.

"What is remarkable about MCA is that in Johor in 2018 we did not win a single seat, but in the 2022 state election we won four seats — all taken from DAP. This time we won another four, bringing the total to eight, and for the first time we surpassed the number of seats won by DAP. This is an achievement.

"But we must not get carried away with this success, because we still have a bigger mission. We need to consolidate more programmes to win the areas where we lost by a narrow margin. For example at the Stulang state seat, we lost by just over 600 votes," he said.
He said the same approach needed to be applied in Melaka and other states, with MCA identifying its strengths and potentially winnable seats based on precise analysis.
"If you have not started yet, find a place to start. We need to prepare early.
"We cannot be the kind of party that only gets ready today because we are contesting tomorrow. That is not the way," he said.

15e890c45de18a1a: BEIJING: China's foreign minister Wang Yi said Beijing was willing to "safeguard" Iran's rights during talks with his counterpart Abbas Araghchi on Wednesday, as Beijing seeks to mediate in Tehran's war with the US.
China is "willing to strengthen dialogue and cooperation with Iran, and safeguard Iran's legitimate rights and interests", Wang told Araghchi as they met in the Chinese capital.
"We encourage Iran and the US to stay rational and restrained," he added.
The talks come one week before an expected trip by Chinese President Xi Jinping to Washington, where he will meet US President Donald Trump.
China, a top economic partner of Iran, has long sought a detente in the months-long conflict in the Middle East, which has at times spilled over into neighbouring countries.
"We do not wish to see regional tensions spilling over into Yemen and the Red Sea," Wang said.

Recent fighting that flared up in Yemen between government forces and the Iran-backed Houthis has displaced more than 100,000 people inside the country while thousands have fled abroad, according to the United Nations.
The war in Iran will be a closely watched topic at Xi's meeting with Trump, among other thorny issues ranging from trade to competition over artificial intelligence.

Beijing refuted this week US media reports that Chinese entities supplied Tehran with satellite images of a military base housing US troops in Jordan, before and after an Iranian strike killed three American soldiers.
Trump has warned Beijing not to sell weapons to Iran, and Washington sanctioned three China-based satellite companies in May for enabling Iran's military operations.
74006a095a051749: STOCKHOLM: Swedish activist Greta Thunberg and other activists have called out British superstar Ed Sheeran after rapper Macklemore was dropped from his tour for making pro-Palestinian comments while performing.

"Ed, there is only one victim here: the Palestinian people," Thunberg, together with activist group Humanti Project, said in post to Instagram late on Tuesday.
According to a post by Sheeran, where he stressed the decision was the promoters, venues on the tour "communicated that they would pull the shows if he was still supporting."

Finneas – a performer also famous for work with his superstar sister Billie Eilish – Irish acts Aaron Rowe and Beoga, and Lukas Graham of Denmark have all posted they were quitting Sheeran's "Loop Tour."

"This is a clear and undeniable sign that the global consciousness has shifted. The normalisation of an apartheid state, and the attempts to sanitise or justify its actions, will no longer be tolerated," the post shared by Thunberg said.
While opening for Sheeran earlier this month at New Jersey's MetLife Stadium, Macklemore shouted "Free Palestine!" and told Palestinians they were "not forgotten."
In his post Tuesday, Sheeran touched on his decision not to comment publicly about political subjects, notably the war in Gaza.
"I am not complicit. I have my personal views on this devastating conflict. Just because I choose not to speak publicly, it doesn't mean I don't care," he said.
Macklemore, known for hits including "Thrift Shop" and "Can't Hold Us", has long vocally supported Palestinians.
In 2024 he released "Hind's Hall," which pays tribute to Hind Rajab, a five-year-old Palestinian girl whose death sparked a wave of international outrage.

f285b522f3a76154: KUALA LUMPUR: The retail prices of RON97, unsubsidised RON95 and unsubsidised diesel will rise by 35 sen a litre for the Sept 17 to 23 period, according to the Finance Ministry.

Tensions in the Middle East had intensified following more than 200 days of conflict, it said.
"Iran had attacked 10 vessels near the Strait of Hormuz in response to US attacks on five Iranian tankers, while attacks had also spread to Yemen and Saudi Arabia's energy infrastructure.
"Vessel traffic through the Straits of Hormuz had fallen to single-digit levels following the escalation in attacks," MOF said in a statement today.
The situation worsened when drone attacks temporarily halted operations along Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, one of the main routes bypassing the Straits of Hormuz.
Talks between Iran and Gulf countries on the security of shipping routes had also been postponed.
"These developments pushed Brent crude oil prices back above US$100 a barrel, reaching nearly US$110 a barrel during the APM calculation period," MOF said.

"The Madani government will continue to protect the people and businesses from the impact of this global uncertainty, including by maintaining targeted Budi Madani subsidies for eligible users," it said.
Despite the increase in unsubsidised prices, eligible Budi Madani RON95 (Budi95) recipients will continue to pay RM1.99 a litre for RON95.
This means the government will bear a subsidy of RM2.38 a litre, equivalent to 54 per cent of the unsubsidised price of RM4.37.
Eligible Budi Madani Diesel (Budi Diesel) recipients will continue to pay RM2.10 a litre for diesel, compared with the unsubsidised price of RM5.27.
The government subsidy amounts to RM3.17 a litre, or 60 per cent of the unsubsidised price.
The subsidised fuel prices remain as follows:
RON95 (Budi95): RM1.99 a litre
Diesel (Budi Diesel): RM2.10 a litre
Subsidised Petrol Control System (SKPS): RM2.05 a litre
Subsidised Diesel Control System (SKDS): RM2.15 a litre
Through Budi95 and Budi Diesel, eligible Malaysians can continue to purchase subsidised RON95 and diesel using their MyKad, subject to their monthly eligibility limits, MOF said.
It said the basic monthly eligibility limit for BUDI95 and BUDI Diesel had been increased to 300 litres from Sept 1.
Eligible owners of diesel-powered pickup trucks and jeeps will also receive an additional 100 litres, bringing their total monthly eligibility to up to 400 litres.

3ee1f9911a61f2e1: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — As Malaysia approaches the implementation of the Online Safety Act 2025, an important debate is emerging over the legislation’s age verification requirements.

The discussion centres on whether platforms should rely on government-issued identification such as MyKad and MyDigital ID, or adopt a multi-layered age assurance approach that prioritises user privacy while ensuring teen safety.

The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), received substantial feedback during public consultations, with industry and civil society stakeholders broadly advocating flexible, risk-based solutions rather than strict identification requirements.

The consultation received feedback from 21 respondents, including human rights and civil society organisations, such as CIJ and technology companies such as Meta, Google, TikTok Service Pte Ltd, X Corp., Roblox, and Redone, alongside telco providers including Maxis, CelcomDigi, Telekom Malaysia, Time dotCom, YTL Communications and Astro.
To better understand the limitations of such a proposal, Malay Mail spoke to several experts for their views on the legislation.
Potential cybersecurity risks

One of the major concerns surrounding such a rule requiring social media platforms to seek government-issued identification for age verification lies within cybersecurity risks, especially in the event of mass hacks.

United Youth Alliance exco member Na’im Brundage said, “Malaysia has had serious data-security problems, with repeated leaks and breaches involving personal information,” referring to recent hacking incidents of government websites being hacked.
In June, the Health Ministry confirmed its official website was hacked after the portal displayed a message believed to have been left by the attackers.
Na’im also expressed his concerns over censorship and freedom of expression should social media accounts be linked to the personal identity of the user.

“If every social media account can easily be linked to an individual’s identity, that infrastructure could potentially be abused against whistleblowers, journalists, activists or ordinary Malaysians who are critical of those in power.
“That is why I think a multi-layered age-assurance approach deserves serious consideration,” he said.
According to him, less intrusive methods, such as age estimation or account and device signals, could be used first, with stronger verification such as MyKad and MyDigital ID only where necessary.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

The MCMC’s consultation report highlighted significant concerns over mandatory government verification, with many stakeholders worried that it could lead to the creation of centralised databases and increase the risk of security breaches. — Picture by Raymond Manue
Concerns over data breaches

The MCMC’s consultation report highlighted significant concerns over mandatory government verification, with many stakeholders worried that it could lead to the creation of centralised databases and increase the risk of security breaches.
Centre for Independent Journalism (CIJ) executive director Wathshlah G. Naidu expressed strong opposition to linking social media use with national identification documents.
“This should not be an ID verification approach but an age-assurance approach,” she said.
Wathshlah also raised concerns over how information would be protected, particularly in the event of a data breach.
“MyDigital ID sits in a vacuum of agencies not covered under the Personal Data Act,” she said.

While Wathshlah highlighted the potential drawbacks of mandatory verification, Children’s Commissioner at the Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (Suhakam) Associate Professor Mohd Al Adib Samuri, highlighted that MyKad information could be leaked, stolen or misused.
Wathshlah pointed out that such requirements could exclude marginalised users, adding that the move could worsen digital exclusion and deepen existing divides.
“We will exclude a large number of users who don’t have national IDs, including stateless children, asylum seekers and refugees,” she said.
Privacy and surveillance issues
Wathshlah highlighted the risks of increased surveillance that could arise from linking social media accounts to national IDs.
“There is a huge potential for increased profiling based on who is using social media,” she said.
She cautioned that this profiling could lead to biases and increased governmental oversight of users’ online activities.

“Civil society organisations that rely on social media for advocacy would open themselves up to heightened surveillance,” she warned, highlighting potential implications for freedom of expression and censorship.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Wathshlah suggested a multi-layered approach, which begins with self-declarations and incorporates behavioural analysis for users who may misrepresent their ages. — Picture by Hari Anggara
Alternative rights-respecting and privacy-preserving approach
Wathshlah suggested a multi-layered approach, which begins with self-declarations and incorporates behavioural analysis for users who may misrepresent their ages.
“If that system fails, platforms could impose more stringent scrutiny,” she said, stressing that an inclusive age verification framework must balance safety with privacy.
Wathshlah also noted that any framework must be comprehensive, taking into account pre-implementation, execution and post-implementation stages to identify and address potential risks.

Echoing similar sentiments, Malaysian United Democratic Alliance (Muda) head of communications Shah Fariq Aizal Sha Ghazni emphasised the need to implement the most suitable solutions from the outset.
“We must be careful that in trying to solve one problem, we do not create another problem by normalising excessive collection of personal data,” he said.
Fariq also stressed the importance of prioritising privacy, urging the exploration of privacy-preserving approaches.
How are other countries doing it?
Singapore is planning new legislation for early 2027 that will mandate strict teen safeguards.

The country has so far avoided a blanket ban; instead, the government has introduced measures requiring major social media platforms to reduce children’s exposure to harmful online content and improve safety features.
Under the proposed rules, platforms would have to improve controls over how teenagers interact with strangers online.
In European Union, the General Data Protection Regulation requires platforms to obtain explicit consent before gathering data.

The law gives citizens the right to be forgotten, or better known as the “right to erasure”, forcing platforms to delete their data upon request and protecting against the unauthorised misuse of identity under certain conditions.

c82dffe58c4164af: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's Lim Pei Yao and Aw Jian Ting face an uphill task after finishing 27th and 34th respectively in the fencing seeding round of the women's and men's modern pentathlon at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games.
Pei Yao finished 27th out of 33 competitors after recording nine victories and 23 defeats from her 32 bouts.
The Malaysian incurred no penalty points and finished level on nine wins with Hong Kong's Liu Hei Yu and Kyrgyzstan's Marija Shtukina.
Pei Yao, however, finished ahead of both rivals on the tiebreaker after recording two victories in the tied group, with Liu 28th and Shtukina 29th.
Jian Ting, meanwhile, was 34th out of 36 competitors after managing seven victories and 28 defeats from 35 bouts.
He was level on seven wins with United Arab Emirates' Abdllah Mohammad Abdalrhman, but was placed behind him after the Emirati recorded one victory in the tied group compared with none for Jian Ting.
The seeding results determine the athletes' positions for the fencing direct-elimination phase of the semi-final.
Pei Yao and Jian Ting will need to make the most of that stage before moving on to the obstacle event and 100m freestyle swimming.
The points accumulated from the subsequent disciplines will then determine their positions and starting gaps for the final laser run, where the first athlete across the line wins the competition.
Pei Yao will have to climb from 27th in the seeding while Jian Ting faces an even bigger challenge from 34th as they bid to stay in contention for a place in the final.
22514eb9cc89f96d: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 16 — The Selangor government will review follow-up measures to address the deteriorating haze situation, said Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
He said the matter would be discussed in detail, based on reports from all relevant parties, at the Selangor State Executive Council meeting scheduled for Friday.

“This Friday we have an exco meeting. We will carefully discuss the follow-up measures, because after it (haze) cleared a bit on Sunday, the situation worsened again, especially yesterday and today. We will see on Friday according to reports from all parties,” he said.
He said this to reporters after officiating the Festival Turath Islami Malaysia 2026, at Masjid Putra here today, which was held in conjunction with the Festival Turath Islami Malaysia 2026.

317c5a615f7d57b1: PETALING JAYA: Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir’s removal as Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan in April was legitimate, says the Negeri Sembilan executive council.
In a statement, the council said Tuanku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja'afar was therefore the new ruler of Negeri Sembilan.
FMT has reached out to menteri besar Ismail Lasim to confirm the statement.

It said the council, chaired by Ismail, convened yesterday and collectively decided that the April 19 proclamation for the removal of Tuanku Muhriz had been signed and sealed by the duly constituted and incumbent undangs.
“The proclamation was also signed by the menteri besar on Aug 3, thereby rendering the proclamation complete in accordance with Article 10(2) of the Negeri Sembilan constitution,” it said.
The state executive council also said that the proclamation of Tunku Nadzaruddin as the new Yang Dipertuan Besar was valid and properly made under the Negeri Sembilan constitution.
“The state government shall take immediate steps to implement the decisions set out in this announcement,” it said.

This comes two days after the Negeri Sembilan Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) maintained that Tuanku Muhriz remains the state's ruler and that the latest attempt to remove him earlier this month was invalid.
At a press conference with three other undangs in April, the purported Sungai Ujong undang Mubarak Dohak announced the removal of Tuanku Muhriz as state ruler.
Two months later, Tuanku Nadzaruddin was proclaimed as the 12th Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan in a ceremony at a five-star hotel in Melaka.
Last week, the four purported undangs produced a proclamation to remove Tuanku Muhriz as Yang Dipertuan Besar, signed by Ismail.

Ismail however said he was coerced into signing the proclamation, maintaining that the document was invalid. However, a lawyer representing the four purported Negeri Sembilan chieftains disputed Ismail's claim, describing it as a mere afterthought.

The DKU on Monday said it had instructed its secretary to file a police report over a statement by the Secretariat of the Four Undangs calling on the state administration to comply with a proclamation to remove the state ruler.
bd0252f577b821b7: KUALA LUMPUR: Media Prima Berhad's (MPB) "Wajah Malaysia" mobile truck drew visitors at the 2026 Keretapi Sarong event at The Exchange TRX here today with free personalised newspaper front-page prints and interactive activities.

cd820ba569501434: THE HAGUE: Former Kosovo president Hashim Thaci was found guilty of war crimes including murder, torture and illegal detention by the Kosovo war crimes tribunal on Wednesday.
Thaci, 58, was sentenced to 25 years in prison for crimes committed as top commander of the ethnic Albanian Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) during the territory's violent break from Serbia in the 1990s.
The tribunal said he was guilty of the murder of 96 political opponents and perceived collaborators with Serbian security forces by Kosovo Liberation Army forces during the conflict.
He was also convicted for the arbitrary illegal detention of 385 people, torture of 303 people and cruel treatment of around 50.
The court said Thaci had "actively participated in and encouraged crimes".
Thaci, who stood in silence as the judge read out the conviction and the sentence, had denied all charges.

The ruling was closely watched in Kosovo and Serbia, where the legacy of the 1998-99 conflict and Kosovo's 2008 declaration of independence remain a source of tension between ethnic Kosovo Albanians and Serbs.
Thaci remains a revered figure for many Kosovo Albanians, while the tribunal itself is deeply unpopular in Kosovo.
In Pristina, thousands of people watching the verdict on a big screen booed the verdict and chanted "Thaci, Thaci" as some burst into tears.
Outside the Kosovo Specialist Chambers in The Hague dozens of Thaci supporters had gathered ahead of the verdict waving KLA flags and chanting "UCK", the Albanian acronym for the army.

cc8d1ec1ae18b49f: KUALA LUMPUR: National doubles coaching director Rexy Mainaky has urged senior shuttlers, including Chen Tang Jie, Pearly Tan and M. Thinaah, to revisit the best moments of their careers ahead of the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games.
Tang Jie won Malaysia's first mixed doubles world title with Toh Ee Wei at the 2025 World Championships, but the latter is recovering from knee surgery in Melbourne.
World No. 5 Pearly-Thinaah were also Malaysia's first women's pair to win a silver medal at the same event.
While Tang Jie will face the Asian Games challenge with new partner Cheng Su Yin, a back injury sustained in April has also affected Pearly's form, with the top Malaysian pair struggling for results.
However, Rexy believes revisiting the players' finest moments through extensive video analysis will help refresh their minds before the competition begins on Sunday.

"Perhaps when we are there, we will spend more time refreshing them on what has worked well in their performances so far, particularly for Tang Jie, and Pearly, Thinaah and Low Zi Yu," said Rexy at the Academy Badminton Malaysia before departing for Japan today.
"We want to use those positive performances as a source of motivation for them.
"We may also arrange additional training sessions. For example, if our main training is in the afternoon, we may ask some of the players to come to the court earlier in the morning.
"We can then look at what we have seen from the videos and work on specific areas that need to be touched up before the start of our first tie.

"I have already spoken to Tang Jie, Pearly, Thinaah and Zi Yu. I have yet to speak to the men's doubles players, but they already have their sessions, and I believe they already have the right mindset.
"This process will include reviewing both the videos and our discussions with the players.
"I'm refreshing this for them so they can look back at their previous performances and understand why they played the way they did.
"We're not only looking at their style of play, but also how they behave, think and respond on court. We need to look at all of that as well.
"The video sessions will also allow us to analyse many different angles, for example, handling each point and responding to their partner during play."

The BA of Malaysia has set a target of one silver and one bronze medal, with men's doubles pairs Goh Sze Fei-Nur Izzuddin Rumsani and Aaron Chia-Tee Kai Wun, Pearly-Thinaah, as well as Tang Jie-Su Yin expected to fight for medals.
Malaysia won a bronze medal at the 2022 Hangzhou Games through Aaron Chia-Soh Wooi Yik, but the latter has been left out of the squad.
Despite the odds, Rexy remains confident his senior players can deliver a medal-winning performance in Japan if they rediscover the form that helped them produce excellent results in the past.
The Asian Games badminton competition starts with the team event on Sunday.

0fbc68b2219242e8: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's transition to a 5G dual network model is entering a critical phase, with mobile network operators (MNO) set to begin equity accounting for Digital Nasional Bhd's (DNB) financials in the fourth quarter (Q4) of financial year 2026 (FY26).
The move could provide greater clarity on the impact of DNB's financial and operational performance on the earnings and dividend outlook of its MNO shareholders, according to Kenanga Research.
CelcomDigi Bhd, Maxis Bhd and YTL Power International Bhd each hold a 33.3 per cent stake in DNB - and its equity accounting treatment is expected to materialise in Q4.

Kenanga Research said the developments of the dual network are largely reflected in CelcomDigi's current valuation as the stock is trading below its historical mean, and therefore offering greater downside protection.
"This, coupled with its more attractive risk-reward, makes CelcomDigi our preferred MNO play over Maxis.
"Under our bear and bull scenarios, CelcomDigi offers 37 per cent upside and 26 per cent downside, compared with 21 per cent upside and 20 per cent downside for Maxis," it said.

Kenanga Research said Maxis has less valuation cushion, as it already trades at historical mean. This reflects its stronger earnings delivery which helped support a reversal in consensus earnings downgrades since early-2025.
"Increasingly, we believe that earnings delivery, alongside 5G dual network developments, will be a key driver of MNO share price performance from hereon," it added.
Kenanga Research expects CelcomDigi's earnings to improve in the near term, as its targeted post-merger synergies are not fully reflected in either the firm's forecasts or consensus estimates.
"Faster-than-expected realisation of these savings could therefore catalyse a reversal in consensus earnings downgrades and support a recovery in valuation multiples.
"Consequently, CelcomDigi offers greater scope for positive earnings surprises relative to Maxis, in our view," it added.
Separately, Kenanga Research said it is less concerned about potential near-term DNB-related funding requirements, as its analysis suggests that both MNOs have ample balance-sheet capacity.
This enables them to absorb additional funding requirements in the near term without materially compromising their dividend capacity.
The bigger risk will be if shareholder funding becomes a long-term recurring commitment, persisting until DNB reaches sustainable cash-flow breakeven.
The firm kept its "Neutral" call on the sector, with an "Outperform" call on CelcomDigi (target price: RM3.28) and "Market Perform" call on Maxis (target price: RM3.70).
bbb501c171a828bc: JAKARTA: Indonesia has sealed off 50 companies across eight provinces after forest and land fire hotspots were identified within their operational areas.
Deputy Environment Minister Diaz Hendropriyono said the move was part of law enforcement efforts, with authorities monitoring the firms to determine their involvement in the blazes.

"We are monitoring these companies and 50 have now been sealed off. This means there were fires there, and if it is proven that the companies were involved, sanctions will be imposed," he said, as reported by the Antara news agency today.

Meanwhile, the Forestry Ministry said 1,037 high-confidence hotspots were detected nationwide as of 9.05pm local time on Tuesday. This represents a drop of 400, or about 27.8 per cent, from 1,437 a day earlier, according to data from its SiPongi monitoring system.

Social media updates from the ministry showed that among the six priority provinces, Central Kalimantan recorded 266 hotspots, South Sumatra 245, South Kalimantan 72, Jambi 62, West Kalimantan 43, and Riau 15.
Hotspot numbers declined in Central, West, and South Kalimantan, while increases were recorded in South Sumatra, Jambi, and Riau, requiring continued intensive monitoring.
Joint teams are carrying out patrols, field inspections, and firefighting operations, supported by water bombing, aerial patrols, and weather modification operations where necessary.

Separately, Forestry Minister Raja Juli Antoni urged communities, farmers, and companies to remain vigilant against forest and land fires until late October or early November, warning that natural rainfall is expected to arrive later than previously forecast.

Citing updated forecasts from Indonesia's Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency (BMKG), Raja Juli said rainfall previously expected in early October could be delayed until late October or early November.
"This means the very strong El Nino, similar to the one in 2015, will remain with us for about another one and a half months," he said.
bdaee3f652d645f3: BEIJING, Sept 16 — China opened a major canal today that will provide landlocked areas with direct access to the sea, state media said, reducing transport times and costs as the country aims to bolster trade ties with regional neighbours.
The 134-kilometre Pinglu Canal took four years to build and links Nanning, in the southern manufacturing region of Guangxi, to the Gulf of Tonkin, flanked by China and Vietnam.

Goods from south-western China previously had to be transported to the southern metropolis of Guangzhou in order to reach the sea, but the new canal will cut the journey by more than 560 kilometres, state news agency Xinhua said.
The canal will also reduce transport costs by 18 to 30 per cent, and generate annual savings of more than five billion yuan (RM3.01 billion) in the sector, it added.
State broadcaster CCTV broadcast footage of the first barge to pass through the canal and aerial video of ships navigating its calm waters, describing the waterway as “the project of our century”.
The canal “opens up the shortest, most economical and most convenient route” to Southeast Asia and will boost economic development, Xinhua said.
The new route is particularly important to rural parts of Sichuan, Chongqing and Yunnan, among others, which are less well-connected than more prosperous regions in eastern China.
Coal, ore, cereals, chemicals, agricultural produce and other materials will now be able to reach foreign markets more easily.
The bulk of the canal’s construction work involved widening, deepening and modifying existing waterways, while a small section had to be excavated, Xinhua said.
The project, which began in August 2022, cost a total of 72.7 billion yuan, it added. — AFP
